overview.title: One field. Six connected perspectives.
overview.lede: Security capability emerges from data, training, and the systems that turn model outputs into verified action.
abstract: Advances in language understanding, code reasoning, and tool use are enabling cybersecurity agents to progress from question answering and single-step analysis to vulnerability research, incident investigation, and multistage task execution. This survey examines research on Large Language Models (LLMs) for cybersecurity across six dimensions: **data, training, models, agent systems, evaluation, and applications**.

We argue that cybersecurity LLMs are progressing **from acquiring domain knowledge to learning how to perform interactive tasks**. Task quality and cost depend on both the model and its harness: the model reasons and selects actions, while the harness organizes information, tools, and execution state.

insights.head: One framework, six dimensions
insights.text: Connects data, training, models, agent systems, evaluation, and applications through inputs, outputs, updates, validation, and resource use.

insights.head: Cross-study comparisons
insights.text: Examines how domain adaptation depends on the task, how harnesses shape model behavior, and how validation limits operational benefit.

insights.head: Resources and a research agenda
insights.text: Organizes security datasets, models, agents, and benchmarks, and sets open questions in agentic training and model–harness optimization.

sections.title: From raw data to verified experience
sections.lede: Build data for the learning objective. Preserve provenance, validate outcomes, and keep training separate from evaluation.

points.text: Instructions, reasoning traces, and preference pairs turn documents into task supervision.

points.head: Environments and trajectories

points.head: Validation and separation
points.text: Check executable outcomes and split related code, patches, and reports together.

sections.title: Train for knowledge, judgment, and action
sections.lede: Different objectives build different capabilities. Validated experience connects training stages to later improvements.

sections.lede: Specialized and general-purpose models converge through code, reasoning, and interaction. Their value remains task-dependent.

sections.title: From one answer to a chain of decisions
sections.lede: The harness organizes plans, tools, memory, and verification—and decides when to act, recover, or stop.

figures.caption: Runtime mechanisms and environment interfaces for cybersecurity agents. Planning and tool interaction, retrieval from memory, and outcome validation support ongoing task execution through interfaces to cyber ranges and security investigation and response systems.

figures.caption: Multi-view malware analysis and behavior interpretation. Analysis of the illustrative application wallpaper.apk combines static code, call relationships, execution traces, and UI state to examine SMS-sending behavior and its triggering conditions for analyst review.
figures.summary: Connect code, call relations, execution traces, and UI behavior.

figures.caption: Three execution structures for cybersecurity agents: fixed workflows with predefined steps, dynamic single agents that revise actions based on observations, and multi-agent systems that coordinate through role allocation and shared state.

points.head: Paired versions expose shortcuts
points.text: Require correct decisions on both vulnerable and repaired versions—not just high single-sample F1.

points.head: Clues change completion
points.text: BountyBench and ProtoArena show how task scope and supplied clues change completion rates.

points.head: Separate model from harness
points.text: Keep the model fixed when measuring gains from tools, orchestration, or shared state.

points.head: Report cost with success
points.text: Report success alongside cost, time, and steps; better coverage need not mean lower cost.

sections.title: Turn findings into accepted outcomes
sections.lede: Practical value depends on validated deliverables, human review, and the work saved across the full response cycle.

points.head: Repair & regression
points.text: Check builds, vulnerability regression, functionality, dependencies, and maintainer acceptance.

points.head: Alert to response
points.text: Correlate users, hosts, and events before moving from an alert to an approved response.

points.head: Traceable conclusions
points.text: Ground malware and forensic conclusions in behavior, records, and a reliable timeline.

points.head: Measure total work
points.text: Track useful discoveries, review burden, erroneous responses, and time to deployment.

sections.title: Faster discovery. A different bottleneck.
sections.lede: As discovery accelerates, reproduction, repair, and deployment become critical—and agents join the security boundary.

figures.caption: Backlog dynamics across vulnerability discovery, validation, repair, and deployment. B(t), D(t), and F(t) count outstanding items at the start of a period, newly confirmed items, and items resolved during that period; the counting unit is a vulnerability–affected-asset pair.
figures.summary: Discovery removes risk only when validated findings reach remediation.

figures.caption: Trust boundaries and human intervention in cybersecurity agents. An alert-investigation example illustrates external-content handling, memory provenance, action authorization and human approval, and independent validation of conclusions.
figures.summary: Keep untrusted content, permissions, and independent verification on clear boundaries.

points.head: Measure remediation
points.text: Count accepted repairs, deployment time, and exposure duration alongside discoveries.

points.head: Agents are part of the boundary
points.text: Treat external content as untrusted; apply least privilege and independent verification.

points.head: Hand off with the evidence
points.text: Escalate uncertainty with original evidence, completed checks, and the consequences of each option.

directions.title: Adversarial interaction drives intelligence; intelligence advances security.
directions.lede: Four directions from Section 9.8 for turning stronger capability into lasting security benefit.

items.head: AI-native security architectures
items.text: Build perception, reasoning, decisions, and feedback learning in from the outset; validated experience feeds further learning.

items.head: Transferable failure recovery
items.text: Diagnose invalid hypotheses, tool faults, and interrupted paths, then choose alternatives while retaining useful findings.

items.head: Alternating model–harness updates
items.text: Revise the harness from failures, update the model on the resulting interactions, and test whether gains transfer.

items.head: From discovery to remediation
items.text: Track backlogs, confirmed and resolved issues, review hours, and exposure duration over time.
